Task: Pose transfer combined with virtual try-on — re-pose the person from Image 2 into the pose
of Image 1, then dress them in the garment from Image 3.

## Input roles (strictly enforced)

Image 1 = POSE REFERENCE ONLY.
Take from it exclusively: skeletal joint angles, limb placement, body orientation, torso twist,
head rotation, hand and finger configuration, and camera viewpoint.
Discard from it everything else: sketch / line-art rendering, mannequin appearance, shading,
annotations, arrows, labels, background, and above all its garment silhouette. Do not import any
clothing shape, width or length from Image 1.

Image 2 = IDENTITY AND SCENE REFERENCE.
Preserve: identity, facial geometry, facial features, skin tone and texture, hairstyle and hair
color, age, expression, body proportions, photographic style, background, ambient lighting.
Preserve everything from Image 2 EXCEPT the clothing — the clothing must be fully replaced.

Image 3 = GARMENT REFERENCE ONLY.
Take from it exclusively the garment: category, silhouette, cut, colorway, fabric texture and
sheen, collar / cuff / hem design, buttons, zippers, pockets, stitching, print pattern,
embroidery, logo and lettering.
Discard from it any person, body, mannequin, pose, hairstyle or background.

## Execution order

1. POSE — Transfer Image 1's pose onto the subject of Image 2. Match the reference pose as closely
   as possible with anatomically correct joints, coherent limb lengths, realistic balance and
   weight distribution. No bent-backward limbs, no missing or extra fingers, no fused hands.
   Use Image 1 only as a skeleton and joint relationship; the body's outer silhouette must follow
   the body of Image 2 and the cut of the garment in Image 3.

2. UNDRESS THEN REDRESS — Completely remove the outfit worn in Image 2, then put on the garment
   from Image 3. Do not layer the new garment over the old one, do not leave the old collar,
   sleeve edges, waistband or hemline visible. Neckline, sleeve length, hem position and overall
   coverage are defined by Image 3 only.

3. GARMENT FIDELITY — Reproduce the Image 3 garment 1:1: identical hue and value, fabric sheen,
   thickness, seam placement, trim geometry, pattern scale, pattern position, logo shape and
   lettering. Do not restyle, recolor, redesign, lengthen, shorten or "improve" it. Do not mirror,
   rotate or re-tile the print.

4. FIT AND PHYSICS — The garment must adapt to the new pose with real cloth behaviour: gravity
   drape, natural tension lines, believable folds at shoulders, elbows, waist and hips, shoulder
   seams sitting on the shoulder points, correct sleeve length, compression and wrinkling where
   the body bends, slight fabric occlusion where limbs overlap. No floating cloth, no clipping
   through the body, no flat decal-like pasting.

5. IDENTITY LOCK — The face must read as the exact same individual as Image 2. Do not beautify,
   slim, reshape, age, or apply smoothing or stylization. Keep pores, texture and natural skin
   imperfections.

6. SCENE AND LIGHT INTEGRATION — Keep Image 2's camera perspective, framing, focal length, depth
   of field, background, light direction and color temperature. The garment must be lit by the same
   light source as the face, with matching shadow softness, and must cast coherent shadows onto the
   body while the arms cast coherent shadows onto the garment.

7. STYLE — Render in the photographic style of Image 2. Never render as line art, sketch,
   wireframe, 3D mannequin or annotated figure.

Output: photorealistic composite, sharp focus, accurate colour, natural skin texture, high resolution.

Negative: wrong person, altered or swapped face, different identity, plastic beauty-filter skin,
any remnant of Image 2's original outfit, new garment layered over old clothing, garment from
Image 3 missing or partially applied, redesigned or recolored garment, wrong pattern scale,
mirrored print, distortion of logo lettering, line-art style, sketch lines, mannequin appearance,
annotations, labels, arrows, extra fingers, fused hands, bent-backward limbs, distorted anatomy,
floating cloth, cloth clipping through body, decal-like pasted clothing, inconsistent lighting
direction, mismatched color temperature, watermark, text
